comment: No building elevation sheets or dimension callouts showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to Buildings 7 and 8. Provide registered surveyor elevation data and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) routing along and crossing the site. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows this OHE line running along the southern boundary of the property. Buildings 7 and 8 are positioned closest to this southern boundary. However, no clearance dimension lines or annotations are provided on either the site plan or any building elevation sheets showing the horizontal distance from the buildings' exterior walls or projections to the OHE conductor. No profile/section views are provided showing vertical clearances. The plans do not identify whether the OHE line is a primary, secondary, or neutral conductor, nor is there a surveyed elevation of the conductor provided. No dimension callouts originate from the conductor location itself—the critical measurement baseline required by code.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric conductors. This measurement must be from the outside conductor, not from the pole. The applicant has not provided evidence that this clearance is maintained. Without (1) building elevation sheets showing surveyed conductor elevations, (2) dimension annotations from the outside conductor to the building face, or (3) a registered surveyor's proximity survey per UCM § 1.10.3, the reviewer cannot determine whether the requirement is met. The conservative approach is to flag this as unclear pending submittal of required elevation documentation and proximity survey data.

comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey provided showing distances from proposed parking areas and site features to outside conductor of OHE line. Provide proximity survey documenting radial clearances from all customer facilities.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and site features on southern portion near OHE line
observation: Sheet 4 shows existing OHE line with associated utility poles. Sheet 9 shows the same OHE line routing along the southern boundary with parking areas, driveways, and site improvements in close proximity. The plans do not specify whether the overhead line serves distribution or transmission function, nor are the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) identified. No dimension annotations are provided showing distances from site facilities (parking, driveways, retaining walls) to the outside conductor. A registered surveyor proximity survey documenting existing and proposed facility locations relative to the OHE line is not provided.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (parking, driveways, site improvements) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The distinction between distribution and transmission affects the applicable clearance standard. Without a registered surveyor proximity survey showing the conductor type, voltage level, and radial distances from all proposed facilities, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant has not submitted this required documentation.

comment: No building elevation or profile sheets provided showing vertical clearances from Building 8 roof and overhangs to overhead electric line. Provide engineered building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Building 8 roof and overhang areas adjacent to southern OHE line
observation: Sheet 9 shows Building 8 positioned adjacent to the southern boundary where the OHE line is routed. However, no building elevation or section views are provided on the site plan set that show the roof elevation of Building 8, any rooftop projections (overhangs, canopies, HVAC penetrations, vents), or their vertical clearance from the overhead line. No profile sections are provided showing the relationship between building projections and the conductor location. Building height is specified as 36'-1" but the finished floor and roof elevations are not dimensioned relative to the OHE line.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance (horizontal) and implies vertical clearance verification for any building projections. Without profile or elevation sheets showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the building roof/overhang elevation dimensioned relative to that conductor, compliance cannot be determined. The applicant must provide elevation views with clearance dimensions for all building projections near the overhead line.

comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are missing. Provide building elevation drawings showing surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE line; entire site with overhead facilities
observation: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. The README index lists sheets 1-39 as site/civil engineering and landscape drawings, with no architectural elevation sheets shown. Existing overhead electric lines are depicted on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) and Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan), but no surveyed conductor elevation data is provided on any sheet. No registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements are documented. The electrical survey required by Austin Energy Design per UCM § 1.10.3 does not appear to have been submitted.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires that surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The applicant has not submitted any building elevation sheets. This is a mandatory documentation requirement for any site with buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. The absence of this required documentation constitutes a deficiency regardless of actual clearances that might exist on the ground.

comment: No section/profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to buildings and site features. Provide detailed section and plan views with dimension callouts from outside conductor to building edges and site improvements.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking areas; all structures within clearance distance of OHE line
observation: No section or profile view exhibits are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and site improvements. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows the OHE line and buildings in plan view only, without any profile views. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows contours and building FFEs but does not show overhead conductor elevation or clearance dimensions. No enlarged plan details with cross-section views have been submitted showing the relationship between conductors and building edges, parking surfaces, or driveways.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires dimension lines from the outer conductor to outermost building edges in plan and section views to verify clearance compliance. These dimension annotations are mandatory and must originate from the actual conductor location, not from the pole. The complete absence of section and profile exhibits with clearance dimensions is a deficiency. The applicant must provide these required exhibits.

comment: No documented vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to overhead electric line. Provide grading plan section views with finished elevations at OHE line crossing and surveyed conductor height; specify truck traffic classification.
applicableAreas: Internal driveways and parking areas on southern portion of site where OHE line is routed
observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows finished floor elevations and site contours but does not provide finished driveway grade elevations at specific locations relative to the OHE line shown on Sheet 9. No section views are provided showing the vertical relationship between the lowest point of the overhead electric line and the finished grade of parking/drive areas. Truck traffic classification (which determines 16-foot vs. 18-foot clearance requirement) is not specified on the plans. No mid-span clearance measurements from a registered surveyor are provided.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for parking without truck traffic, or 18-foot with truck traffic, from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including service drops and telecommunications attachments). Without (1) documented finished grade elevations at driveway locations, (2) surveyed overhead line heights, and (3) specification of truck traffic usage, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant must provide site/utility profile views with documented vertical clearances.

comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on site plans, measured from outside conductor as required. All clearance dimensions must originate from the actual conductor location, with notation showing measurement source.
applicableAreas: All locations with clearance dimensions shown on overhead electric facilities
observation: Sheet 9 shows the OHE line on the southern boundary of the site but includes NO dimension callouts or clearance annotations of any kind. Wherever clearance dimensions should appear (from conductor to buildings, parking, driveways), none are provided. The few dimension lines visible on Sheet 9 relate to building setbacks and site distances, not to overhead line clearances. The critical requirement to show dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not pole centerline) is therefore not met—because no dimensions are shown at all.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires clearance dimensions to be measured from the outside conductor, never from the utility pole centerline. On multi-conductor installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center, creating significant measurement errors if pole-based dimensions are used. The applicant has not provided any clearance dimensions from any overhead electric infrastructure. This is a foundational deficiency—without dimension callouts originating from the conductor, the plans cannot communicate or verify clearance compliance.

comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided despite buildings and parking areas being positioned adjacent to overhead electric line. Provide licensed surveyor measurements of overhead conductor heights and clearances to all proposed structures and site features.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking and driveway areas adjacent to southern OHE line
observation: Sheet 4 shows an existing OHE line with utility poles routed across the property. Sheet 9 shows Buildings 7 and 8 and parking/driveway areas positioned immediately adjacent to this overhead line (on southern boundary). Without seeing surveyed conductor elevations or documented clearance measurements, the vertical clearance appears potentially marginal—the minimum required clearances (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18-foot for driveways, 7.5-foot for parking) cannot be visually confirmed from plan-view drawings alone. No mid-span clearance survey data from a registered surveyor is provided to document actual measured clearances.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements or when visual determination is insufficient. Given the close proximity of buildings and parking to the OHE line shown on the plans, and the complete absence of vertical clearance documentation, a registered surveyor's measurement is required to verify compliance. The applicant has not provided this required survey work.

comment: Mitigation trees shown on landscape plan adjacent to overhead electric line lack species identification and utility-compatible designation. Identify all mitigation tree species and confirm UC (Utility Compatible) status per ECM Appendix F, or relocate trees to maintain 10-foot minimum lateral clearance from outside conductor.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary landscaping area with overhead electric line; mitigation tree plantings
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) running along the southern boundary. Multiple mitigation trees (labeled 'M' on the plan) are positioned directly along this southern boundary, within or immediately adjacent to (less than 10 feet lateral distance from) the overhead line. Sheet 32 (Tree List) identifies the surveyed existing trees with species and Appendix F designation (Y/N/I), but does NOT specify the species of the proposed MITIGATION trees shown as 'M' symbols on Sheet 31. No legend or note on Sheet 31 provides species names for the mitigation plantings. No reference to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible trees (UC designation) appears in the landscape legend. No clearance distance annotations or notes document the required 10-foot lateral separation or specify that utility-compatible species are being used.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors to be from the Utility Compatible tree list in ECM Appendix F (generally species with mature height ≤20 feet marked 'UC'). The applicant's landscape plan shows mitigation trees under the overhead line but does not identify the species. Without species identification, the reviewer cannot verify that utility-compatible trees are being used. The vegetation plan is deficient. The applicant must identify all mitigation tree species and confirm they meet the UC requirements, OR relocate trees to comply with the 10-foot minimum lateral separation for non-utility-compatible species.

comment: Specific 48-hour notification note required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 is not clearly called out on cover sheet or plans. This requirement must be conspicuously noted on site plans. While general Austin Energy notes are present on Sheet 3, the specific 48-hour notification requirement is not clearly set out as a distinct, stand-alone note with notification procedures. Best practice is to include this as a separate, highlighted note on the cover sheet with contact information for Austin Energy notification.

comment: Seven mitigation trees are shown with trunk centers plotted directly on the overhead electric line where utility poles are located, placing them within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone from utility poles.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts seven (7) mitigation trees (marked 'M' designation) plotted with their trunk centers positioned directly at the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern property boundary. Vision analysis confirmed these tree symbols intersect the OHE utility line with zero (0) feet lateral distance measured. Two utility pole symbols (circles with crosses) are shown at the western and eastern ends of this OHE line. Trees are shown directly adjacent to or overlapping these pole locations.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any electric utility pole (measured from trunk center to pole). The landscape plan shows trees with trunk centers plotted at approximately 0 feet from the utility line where poles are located, which is well within the 10-foot prohibited zone. This represents a direct violation of the pole clearance requirement. The vision tool's examination of the plan found no dimension callouts that would indicate these trees are actually set back to compliant distances.

No root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are documented on the landscape plan or landscape detail sheets for any trees within the 20-foot protection zone.

The landscape plan (Sheet 31) provides no callouts, detail references, or notes specifying root barrier requirements for any of the 20 proposed trees or existing trees. Without root barrier documentation on the landscape and detail sheets, compliance with this requirement cannot be verified.

The landscape plan fails to provide species identification for the specific trees shown near the OHE line, making it impossible to verify whether they meet utility-compatible requirements or comply with size restrictions.

comment: No clearance dimensions, measurement lines, or distance callouts are shown on the landscape plan between trees and the overhead electric line or utility poles, preventing verification of compliance with minimum clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
observation: Comprehensive visual examination of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no dimension lines, measurement arrows, or numerical distance callouts between any proposed trees and the overhead electric (OHE) line or utility poles. A detailed scan of the entire sheet confirmed absence of: (1) dimension lines between tree symbols and utility infrastructure, (2) written notes specifying clearances, (3) references to utility clearance requirements, or (4) any measurements related to tree-utility separation. The plan shows the OHE line and tree locations but provides no quantitative clearance verification.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires clearances measured as lateral distance from tree trunk center to the outside conductor. Measurement methodology must be documented on plans to verify compliance. The landscape plan shows trees at the OHE line but provides zero dimensional information. Without clearance dimensions, it is impossible to determine whether trees meet the required distances (15 feet for distribution clearance zones, 10 feet from poles). The absence of any measurement callouts is itself a deficiency.

comment: No clearance dimensions are provided from tree trunk centers (planting locations) to utility conductors. The large canopy circles shown for each tree could be misinterpreted as measurement origins if any dimensions were present.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) displays trees as circular symbols with inner trunk-center points and larger outer circles representing canopy extent. No dimension lines originate from tree trunk centers (the inner circle points representing planting locations). Where tree-utility distances appear to be dimensioned at all (which they are not), any measurement endpoints would be at the canopy edge rather than the planting trunk location. Vision analysis confirmed no measurements of any kind are shown on the plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that clearances must be measured from the tree trunk center (planting location), not from the projected canopy edge. The measurement methodology is critical because measuring from canopy edge significantly underestimates the distance available to utilities. The plan fails on two counts: (1) it provides no measurements at all, and (2) the tree symbols do not include dimension lines that would clarify measurement origin points (trunk vs. canopy).

comment: Trees are shown on the landscape plan in proximity to the overhead electric line, but without clearance dimensions, distance callouts, or specification notes, clearance verification is prevented.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line (OHE) along southern property boundary
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does show the overhead electric (OHE) line and seven proposed trees in visual proximity. However, the plan lacks any clearance verification information: no dimension callouts, no written notes specifying distances or compliance status, no reference to conductor locations for measurement origin, and no identification of the specific tree species for those trees near the OHE line. While trees and utilities are graphically shown together, clearance verification is impossible due to the complete absence of dimensional or specification information required to confirm compliance.
reasoning: The grouping specifies that trees must be 'shown on landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities, preventing clearance verification.' The intent of this requirement is to ensure viewers can verify that the spatial relationship satisfies clearance requirements. Although trees and OHE are displayed on the same drawing, the lack of any dimension, note, or specification information prevents any meaningful verification. Showing trees and utilities on the same sheet without clearance documentation is insufficient for code compliance verification.

comment: Trees are proposed at zero feet from the overhead electric line in direct violation of minimum clearance requirements. No documented written approval from Austin Energy is present on the plans to authorize this variance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line where seven trees are plotted
observation: Seven mitigation trees are shown on Sheet 31 with trunk centers positioned at approximately zero (0) feet lateral distance from the overhead electric (OHE) line. This placement is clearly within the restricted clearance zone (< 15 feet from distribution conductors, < 10 feet from utility poles). No documentation of Austin Energy written approval is present on the landscape plan, electrical plan, site notes, or in the supplementary documents (no letters or approval certificates are referenced or attached). The plans propose trees in prohibited zones with no evidence of required variance authorization.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that 'Variations to planting distances and species identified as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F require explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' Trees proposed within prohibited zones (< 15 feet distribution, < 10 feet poles) must include documented Austin Energy approval. The site plan shows no such approval. Without documented authorization, the proposed tree locations violate the clearance requirements.

comment: All eight building foundations have underground electric conduit routing within 5 feet (typically within 0 to 2 feet) of building walls to serve wall-mounted electrical meters. This violates the required 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations. Either relocate meters to comply with clearance or coordinate with Austin Energy for exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B.
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, scale 1" = 20') reveals that electrical meters are mounted directly on the building foundation walls for all eight buildings. Underground electric conduit and lines routing to these meters are shown running immediately adjacent to (and in some cases directly against) the building foundation walls. Specifically: Building 1 meter on northwest corner wall with conduit running along west foundation; Building 2 meter on south wall with branch line routing directly to recessed area; Building 3 meter on east wall with line running to foundation; Building 4 meter on north wall with line from northeast pull box; Building 7 meter on east wall with conduit from southeast corner; Building 8 meter on north wall (recessed notch) with lines routing along foundations. The electrical conduit serving each meter breaches the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone and runs within inches of the building foundations.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes, manholes) to customer buildings and foundations. The site plan clearly shows electrical meters mounted directly on building walls with underground conduit routed immediately adjacent to building foundations. This is a direct violation of the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. The presence of wall-mounted meters inherently requires conduit to enter the building within the 5-foot zone. This is not a design that coordinates with the clearance requirement—it fundamentally violates it.

comment: Multiple storm drain inlets are proposed within 5 feet of underground electric facilities. Specifically, courtyard inlets conflict with transformer pads, and the inlet west of Building 2 is positioned directly adjacent to the electrical utility line. Revise drain inlet locations to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all underground electric facilities, or coordinate with Austin Energy for encasement/protection measures if clearance cannot be achieved.
applicableAreas: Courtyard area between Buildings 4-7, near Building 2, near Buildings 7-8
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and cross-reference with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals multiple storm drain inlets positioned directly adjacent to or within close proximity of underground electrical infrastructure. Specific conflicts identified: (1) Central courtyard area contains four 18" grate inlets (Rim elevations 683.13, 683.15, 682.95, 683.10) positioned in the central landscaped/hardscape courtyard where transformer pads are located; (2) West of Building 2, an 18" grate inlet (Rim 683.82) is positioned directly adjacent to the "E" (electrical) utility line running along the western boundary; (3) South of Buildings 7 and 8, a series of 2'x2' grate inlets (Rims 679.30, 679.94, 680.99) are located in the drive aisle directly in proximity to electrical infrastructure serving those buildings. These drain inlets are located within the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone required between underground electric facilities and other site improvements.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to site improvements and hardscape features. Storm drain inlets are site drainage improvements that require clearance from electrical infrastructure. The courtyard inlets appear to be directly adjacent to or within the transformer pad areas, and the Building 2 inlet is positioned directly on the electrical line corridor. Visual analysis at the 1" = 20' scale indicates these inlets fall within 5 feet (and likely within 0-3 feet) of the electrical conduit and transformer pads. This represents a coordination failure between drainage design and electrical routing.

comment: Four electrical pull boxes (near Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8) are positioned within 5 feet of building foundations and corners. Relocate pull boxes to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B, or provide justification if clearance maintenance is infeasible and coordinate with Austin Energy Design.
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) reveals electrical pull boxes positioned in close proximity to building foundations at multiple locations: (1) Building 1: Pull box at southwest corner, appearing to be within 5 feet (visually estimated 2-4 feet) of the corner; (2) Building 4: Pull box to the northeast near Unit 404, positioned close to the east foundation line, appearing to be at or near the 5-foot threshold; (3) Building 7: Pull box at southeast corner near Unit 704, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner; (4) Building 8: Pull box at northwest corner near Unit 801, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner. These pull boxes are shown as discrete symbols positioned immediately adjacent to building corners rather than at clear standoff distances.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires pull boxes to maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides, including from building foundations and property lines. Pull boxes are underground electrical facilities that must be accessible for maintenance, and the code establishes clearance from structures to ensure they are not impacted by building foundations or other improvements. The visual positioning of pull boxes at or within building corners (at the 1" = 20' scale) indicates they fail to maintain the required 5-foot clearance zone around them. This is particularly problematic because pull boxes require working space for access and maintenance.

comment: Three storm drain manholes are located directly in pedestrian sidewalk areas and vehicle driveway paths. Relocate manholes to utility easement areas outside of primary circulation routes, or modify site plan to accommodate manhole access without creating conflicts with pedestrian routes, ramps, or vehicle drives.
applicableAreas: Central area between Buildings 7-8, between Buildings 2-3, south of Building 7
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) identifies three storm drain manholes with locations that conflict with pedestrian and vehicular site features: (1) SD Manhole between Buildings 2 and 3 (Rim 684.71): Located in a landscaped/pedestrian area directly adjacent to a north-south sidewalk routing, creating a maintenance access conflict and potential trip hazard in a pedestrian circulation path; (2) SD Manhole between Buildings 7 and 8 (Rim 683.78): Located in a paved pedestrian sidewalk threshold connecting the southern parking area to the central courtyard, directly in a pedestrian travel path; (3) SD Manhole south of Building 7 (Rim 681.02): Located directly in the paved vehicle driveway path, a primary vehicle circulation area. These manhole locations overlap with primary site circulation routes rather than being positioned in dedicated utility access areas.
reasoning: Manhole placement must not conflict with site features that require vertical transitions (stairs, ramps, accessible routes) and should not be located directly in high-traffic pedestrian or vehicular circulation paths. The three manholes are positioned in: one in a pedestrian sidewalk area, one directly in a pedestrian pathway serving multiple buildings, and one in a primary vehicle driveway. These locations create conflicts with site circulation, accessibility, maintenance access, and pose potential trip hazards. Manhole covers in circulation paths are a code compliance issue and accessibility/safety concern.

comment: Underground electric conduit routing to serve wall-mounted electrical meters on all eight buildings would require conduit to pass beneath or through building foundations, which violates UCM § 1.10.5.B. Relocate electrical meters to pedestals or external equipment enclosures outside of building footprints, or coordinate with Austin Energy Design to document a license agreement and sealed engineering design if conduit must pass through building foundations, with metal sleeves allowing replacement.
observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows that underground electric conduit is routed to and directly beneath building foundations to serve electrical meters mounted on building walls. Specifically: (1) All eight buildings have underground electric lines routing to wall-mounted meters; (2) These lines originate from transformers or pull boxes and run directly to the building serving as conduit entry points; (3) The conduit must pass beneath or immediately adjacent to building foundations to reach the meters; (4) In some cases (Buildings 2, 8), the meters are mounted in recessed notches in the building walls, requiring conduit to route into these recessed areas. This represents a direct routing of underground electric facilities beneath building foundations and service areas.
reasoning: Wall-mounted electrical meters inherently require underground conduit to be routed to the building. When buildings are designed with slab-on-grade construction (as noted in the site data), conduit routing beneath the slab violates the prohibition. While some conduit may pass through retaining walls below grade (with an exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B requiring license agreement and engineering), the routing of conduit as the primary service to wall-mounted meters is not addressed by this exception.

comment: Applicant must provide one of the following: (1) Pavement Design Sheets certifying that all roads, driveways, and parking areas within transmission easements are designed to support 48,000 lb tandem axle loads with 5-foot spacing, including subgrade, base, and surface course calculations sealed by a registered engineer, OR (2) Revised site plan with a note explicitly stating that no roads, pavement, driveways, or parking areas are located within the transmission easement areas. comment: Biofiltration/detention pond in the northeast corner is adjacent to overhead distribution electric line on eastern property boundary. The overhead electric line running along the eastern boundary serves distribution facilities (indicated by '-OE-' notation and transformer pads shown on Sheet 21, confirming distribution voltage, not transmission). The requirement is explicit: applicants must demonstrate compliance through professional engineer-certified exhibits showing measured clearances. The pond profiles provided (Sheets 16 Sections A-A and B-B) show pond geometry and internal elevations but do not extend to show the overhead conductors or clearance dimensions. This deficiency requires submission of additional exhibit sheets showing the clearance verification.

comment: Tree plantings shown within electric easements would obstruct 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the 5-foot electric easement boundaries to maintain unobstructed access corridor, or provide engineer certification that design maintains minimum 12-foot clear width for maintenance vehicle access along entire easement length. Easement widths (5 feet) are minimal; tree canopies, trunks, and root systems would occupy much of this width, leaving insufficient space for a maintenance vehicle to traverse the easement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping within electric easements be positioned such that it does not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. The fundamental purpose of an electric easement is to provide Austin Energy with unrestricted access for construction, operation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. Tree plantings shown within the 5-foot easement corridors, with typical canopy spreads of 20-40+ feet (varying by species), would substantially obstruct this required access. Even if a license agreement were in place (which it is not, per EL-5.11), landscaping must be designed to maintain unobstructed access. The current landscape plan does not demonstrate this; trees are shown directly within the easement boundaries.

comment: Permanent wood fencing is shown within 5-foot electric easements on eastern and southern property boundaries. UCM § 1.10.10.2 permits only removable wooden fences under license agreement. Either: (1) remove fencing from easement boundaries and relocate outside easement areas, (2) replace with removable fence type with notation indicating removable design allowing Austin Energy access, or (3) obtain executed license agreement from Austin Energy permitting the fence type proposed. Provide details showing fence construction and removability certification if fences will remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Wood fencing along eastern and southern property boundaries within 5-foot electric easements
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows fencing lines drawn directly along the eastern and southern property boundaries. These same property boundaries have 5-foot electric easements dedicated to utility use (labeled on Sheet 9 as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 60...' on the east and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885...' on the south). The fence lines follow the property boundary, placing them within the 5-foot easement width. The site plan notes describe these as 'Wood Fence' (eastern boundary), consistent with a typical residential privacy fence constructed of wood. Site plan details and notes do not identify these fences as removable, temporary, or specially designed to allow Austin Energy access. Standard residential wood fencing would constitute a permanent, non-removable obstruction within the easement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly allows removable wooden fences within electric easements under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. However, it prohibits permanent or non-removable fencing. The distinction is critical: 'removable wooden fences' implies temporary structures that can be taken down during maintenance, whereas standard residential wood fences (which appear to be shown on Sheet 9) are permanent structures. The submitted plans do not specify that these fences are removable or designed for Austin Energy access. Additionally, there is no documented license agreement for easement use (per EL-5.11), which would be a prerequisite even for removable fencing. The presence of permanent-appearing wood fences within the easements violates the prohibition on non-removable fencing.

comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show existing electric easements with dimension callouts demonstrating clearances from easement boundaries to proposed structures. Provide dimensioned clearance details for all structures located within 15 feet of electric easement boundaries, showing that horizontal sky-to-ground clearance of 7.5 feet and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors are maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.

observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts all buildings and easements but contains NO dimension callouts showing clearances from building structures to electric easement boundaries. reasoning: The grouping requires clearance verification exhibits showing existing electric easements with dimensions from easement boundaries to proposed structures. The site plan adequately shows the location of buildings and easements, but affirmatively demonstrates NO clearance dimensions. While the site plan is otherwise complete, the absence of specific clearance callouts makes compliance verification impossible—the burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate clearance compliance, not on the reviewer to measure unmarked plans. This deficiency applies to all structures within 15 feet (for overhead facilities) of electric easement boundaries. Facts.md further documents that two major easements affecting the northeast corner are not depicted on submitted plans, which directly impacts the ability to verify clearances related to those undepicted easements.

reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 (Application Requirements for Austin Energy Land Development Review) requires that easements serving electric facilities be clearly and properly labeled. comment: Overhead electric facilities are present on the site but are not designated with 'aerial electric easement' label; generic electric easement label used instead. The presence of overhead facilities (-OHE- notation) is confirmed on the plans, but the associated easements are not labeled to denote their aerial nature. applicableAreas: Electric easements on east and south property boundaries; all electric facilities requiring 24/7 access
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a continuous concrete retaining wall running the entire north, east, and south perimeter of the property, physically separating the interior townhome complex from the exterior easement areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'Easements running along the East and South boundaries appear entirely cut off from the public right-of-way (Valley View Road located on far west)... Accessing them from the street requires navigating through private internal drives, bypassing the townhome structures, and traversing the continuous Concrete Retaining Wall.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows NO explicitly labeled access routes (e.g., 'Electric Access Route' or 'Maintenance Path') designated exclusively for electric facilities. While transformer pads on the west side of the property are adjacent to the main driveway loop and are accessible, the 'Electric Easement' areas on the east and south perimeters, as well as pull boxes and other underground facilities in those areas, have no demonstrated access from public ROW. The plan notes 'No explicitly labeled maintenance paths or access routes designated for servicing the electric, telecom, or greenbelt utility easements.'
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 (Access to AE Facilities) and UCM § 1.14.4 (Access—Transmission Facilities) require that Austin Energy maintain permanent, unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access to all electric facilities for installation, operation, and maintenance. The defining requirement is that access must be available from public right-of-way without traversing private property or encountering physical obstructions. The site plan affirmatively demonstrates that easement areas on the east and south are separated from public street access by a continuous retaining wall; access to these areas requires routing through private internal driveway systems and bypassing residential buildings. This configuration fails to provide the 'unobstructed' access required by code. Further, the plan contains no explicit access route designations for electric maintenance, leaving access provisions ambiguous. The grouping's common violation pattern identifies this exact deficiency: 'Access shown but not dimensioned' or 'no access route from public ROW is shown.'

If any electric easement areas are not paved all-weather surfaces, revise grading/landscaping to provide such surfaces or provide written approval from Austin Energy for alternative surface treatment.

observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) delineates easement boundaries (5' Electric Easements, 5' P.U.E., 25' Drainage Easement, etc.) but provides NO explicit surface material specifications (HMAC pavement, PCC concrete, gravel, grass, or unpaved) within the electric easement areas. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes that transformer pads are 'located in spaces containing overlapping circular symbols indicating tree canopies, suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas, though the exact surface material is not named.' The plan shows contours and drainage features within easements but not surface material specifications.
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that drivable surfaces within electric easements be suitable for maintenance vehicles and large bucket trucks. LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines 'all-weather driving surface' as Hot Mix Asphaltic Concrete (HMAC) or Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Grass, gravel, and unpaved surfaces do not qualify. The grading plan is the appropriate sheet to specify these surface materials, but it lacks explicit callouts. While driveways and parking areas shown in the western portion of the site are clearly delineated as paved (implied by curb lines and pavement specifications in construction details), the eastern and southern electric easement areas are not similarly labeled. The absence of explicit surface specification prevents verification of compliance. This creates genuine ambiguity—the surfaces may be paved (meeting code) or unpaved (failing code), but cannot be determined from the submitted plans.

Easement on the south perimeter.' A Wood Fence is labeled running along the far East property line...A Pond Perimeter Fence circles the NE corner pond.' Further, the concrete retaining wall and associated fence structures running through easement boundaries create physical obstructions that prevent equipment access and violate the ground-to-sky clearance requirement. The grouping's common violation pattern explicitly lists this deficiency: 'Site plan shows building overhang, awning, canopy, or permanent structure extending into or over electric easement, violating ground-to-sky clearance requirement.' Here, trees, walls, and fencing occupy that space.

reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and UCM § 1.5.2.1.L require that Public Utility Easements serving electric facilities be kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other permanent improvements without written approval from Austin Energy. The site plan affirmatively shows permanent structures (detention pond with retaining walls and fencing) placed within the 25' Drainage Easement area in the NE corner. The Greenbelt easement situation is even more problematic: it is a perpetual no-build zone per the recorded instrument, yet it was not depicted on the site plan, indicating the applicant either did not account for it in the design or deliberately omitted it. Facts.md explicitly states these easements 'must be depicted before approval' and that 'proposed building layout must be evaluated against both easement footprints.' The combined two easements encumber approximately 0.44 acres (~19% of the 2.16-acre site), yet neither is shown on the submitted plans. This constitutes a fundamental deficiency in PUE documentation and compliance.

comment: It is unclear whether applicant is relying solely on 1975 plat-dedicated easements or proposing new separate-instrument easement dedications for vault and cross-property electric facilities. No separate-instrument exhibits are visible on site plan.
applicableAreas: Vault easement area for transformers; potential cross-property easement areas

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Site Plan Review

observation: This is a site plan filing without concurrent subdivision plat. Existing electric easements from 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat are shown on Sheet 2 (5-foot E&T easement, 7.5-foot P.U.E.) with plat-recorded status. However, additional infrastructure shown on Sheet 21 includes a transformer vault easement (labeled as 'Vault Easement' on the drawing) and an underground electric line that extends across the southern property boundary to an adjacent property. No explicit separate-instrument easement exhibits or dedications are visible on the site plan for these new/modified facilities. The Site Plan Release Notes (Sheet 3, Block 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' suggesting potential future dedications but no current dedicated separate instruments are evident. It is unclear whether the applicant intends to rely solely on the existing 1975 plat easements for all proposed facilities, or whether new separate-instrument dedications are being made for the vault and cross-property facilities.
reasoning: Code §§ 14-1-11, 14-1-21, and 14-1-22 establish that when a site plan is filed without a concurrent platting activity, electric easements must be dedicated by separate recordable document (deed or easement agreement) with metes and bounds and surveyor certification. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site plan is filed without concurrent subdivision plat or when additional easements are needed after plat recordation.' This site IS filed without concurrent plat, AND there ARE additional facilities (vault, cross-property line) shown that may require additional easement dedications beyond what the 1975 plat provides. However, the plans do not clearly indicate whether separate-instrument dedications are being made. The presence of the Bluebeam coordination link with Austin Energy (per master comment report) suggests some coordination occurred, but the visible site plan documents do not show explicit separate-instrument dedications with proper documentation. This ambiguity warrants an 'unclear' determination pending clarification of the applicant's intent regarding separate-instrument dedication.

comment: If new easement dedications are required for vault and cross-property facilities, metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes must be provided to Austin Energy; none are visible on site plan
applicableAreas: Vault easement for transformers; cross-property easement for southern electric line extension
observation: No metes and bounds descriptions, surveyor-sealed field notes, or surveyor exhibits are visible on the site plan for the vault easement (labeled on Sheet 21) or the cross-property electric line extension (shown extending south from the site across property boundary on Sheet 21 vision analysis). The 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat (Sheet 2) shows plat-dedicated easements with surveyor certification dated August 20, 1975, but contains no metes and bounds narrative for those easements—only visual boundary depictions and recording references. If new easement dedications are required (per EL-7.1 determination), Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) mandates that metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes be provided. No such documentation is evident on the submitted site plan sheets.
reasoning: Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) specifies that easement dedications by separate instrument require metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor. UCM § 1.16.0(3) similarly requires that metes and bounds descriptions be provided to Austin Energy for easement dedication. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site requiring electric easement dedication by separate instrument.' If the determination of EL-7.1 is that new separate-instrument dedications ARE required, then metes and bounds are a mandatory component that must be present. The absence of metes and bounds on the visible site plan is a deficiency. However, this determination is contingent on EL-7.1 being clarified as requiring new dedications rather than relying on existing plat easements. Hence, 'unclear' is warranted pending that clarification. If new dedications are required and metes and bounds are absent, this would be a 'fail.'

comment: Transformer vault easements labeled on Sheet 21 but not formally depicted with boundaries, dimensions, or recorded document references as required for proper easement documentation
applicableAreas: Transformer pad vault easement areas (three transformer pads shown on Sheet 21)

The requirement implies that Austin Energy trucks must have direct, unobstructed access to reach the transformer pad. The current configuration shows the pad accessible only via parking lot navigation or via the main driveway, neither of which is documented as a dedicated access route. While the distance technically satisfies the 6-foot requirement, the lack of any dedicated access documentation and the tight confinement of the pad suggest the intent of the requirement (to ensure reliable truck access) may not be met.

comment: Site plan shows entrance and exit gates controlling access to the property. Transformers 2 and 3 are located inside the gated perimeter, preventing 24/7 Austin Energy truck access for emergency response and maintenance. Provide: (1) evidence that all transformers are relocated outside the gated perimeter with direct unrestricted access from Valley View Road, OR (2) a recorded easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 property access regardless of gate status, OR (3) documented written approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing gated access with emergency procedures.

Main entrance driveway and property gates

The controlling provision states 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations' and requires 'Access to AE Facilities' without restriction. Gated residential communities with restricted access prevent Austin Energy trucks from having immediate, unrestricted 24/7 entry to reach transformer equipment during emergencies or for routine maintenance. When transformers are located within a gated property perimeter, Austin Energy requires either: (1) external placement of the transformer outside the gate line with direct truck access, (2) a permanent easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 access regardless of gate status, or (3) a documented AE Design exception authorizing the gated configuration with specific operational procedures. None of these alternatives are documented on the submitted plans.

reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require that transformer pads 'be kept clear of all structures, landscaping, and improvements' to ensure Austin Energy personnel can install, operate, and maintain equipment with appropriate vehicle and personnel access. 'Trees, landscaping, street furniture, dumpster enclosures, water meters, grates, poles, fire hydrants' and other obstructions cannot block access to transformer pads or create safety hazards during equipment servicing. A tree well directly adjacent to the transformer pad represents a site feature that physically obstructs the clear zone and restricts the space available for truck approach, equipment landing, and personnel movement. Tree wells are designed to limit access to protect tree roots; this directly conflicts with the unrestricted access requirement for electrical equipment.

reasoning: The notation of 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Transformer 4 indicates an intent to construct or provide access to underground vault infrastructure. comment: Many meter locations on building faces do not have direct unobstructed line of sight to transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Meters on the east/west/south sides of buildings cannot see transformers on opposite sides. observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to trace visual line-of-sight paths from transformer pads to meter locations. The Regulatory Overview for this grouping clarifies: 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' Line of sight means an unobstructed visual path - if a building structure blocks the direct view from meter to transformer, the line of sight requirement is not met. The vision analysis explicitly identified that 'many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source,' which necessarily means building structures obstruct the line of sight. AE personnel cannot verify connections and perform coordinated operations if they cannot see both the meter and the transformer from a single vantage point.

comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary underground electrical loop, exceeding the maximum of 2 turns permitted by UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q. The rectangular loop configuration around the central buildings necessitates multiple directional changes. Revise the electrical routing design to limit turns between transformer pads and meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends, or provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing the exceeding the standard 2-turn limitation for this site configuration.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing path from transformers to meters throughout site
observation: Examined Sheet 21 to trace electrical routing paths and count 90-degree bends. Vision analysis traced 'the primary electrical routing is denoted by a solid blue line. It enters the site from the mid-western boundary... splits to form a continuous underground loop that follows the inner perimeter of the internal drive aisle, circling the central buildings.' The analysis specifically identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends. Counting just the primary main loop (excluding small jogs to individual pads/meters), there are at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners to navigate the rectangular layout of the site.' The primary electrical loop makes a rectangular circuit around the central buildings, requiring approximately 6 90-degree directional changes (one at each corner of the rectangular loop). Branch connections from this main loop to individual transformers and meters add additional turns.
reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q (Current Transformers and Enclosures) specifies 'maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter.' This limitation is imposed to maintain circuit performance and prevent voltage drop issues. The vision analysis conclusively identified at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary electrical routing loop, which is triple the maximum allowable. The rectangular main loop circuit requires a 90-degree bend at each corner (north, east, south, west), and the perimeter-following design necessitates these turns. This configuration cannot be reconfigured without a complete redesign of the electrical routing topology. The current design violates the maximum two-turn requirement.

comment: Transformer pad 2 is positioned less than 2 feet from a surface parking space, triggering the bollard requirement per UCM § 1.10.4. No bollards are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide: (1) Detail drawing for 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards (per UCM § 1.10.4 standard specification) positioned around Transformer 2, with spacing adequate to allow equipment door openings and access (minimum 3-foot clear width for door swing), OR (2) Reposition Transformer 2 to a location more than 4 feet from all parking spaces and traffic areas.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5, adjacent to parking)
observation: Examined Sheets 21 and 9 to identify transformer pad locations and proximity to parking areas. Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) is positioned immediately adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation per vision analysis: 'T2 is located directly adjacent to a perpendicular surface parking space. It appears to share a boundary or sit mere inches from the northernmost parking space in the cluster west of Bldg. 5. It is absolutely within 6 feet of this parking space.' Sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) was not reviewed but would be the expected location for bollard specifications if they were required and shown elsewhere on the plans.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Bollard requirement when transformer pad is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas... 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards are required and must be spaced to allow equipment door opening.' When transformer equipment is installed less than or equal to 4 feet from a parking space or traffic area, bollards must be provided to prevent vehicles from striking and damaging the transformer. Transformer 2 is less than 2 feet from a parking space, well within the 4-foot trigger distance. This proximity to parking makes the transformer vulnerable to vehicle impact and also creates a safety hazard for parked vehicles in an adjacent space that is separated only by the thin equipment pad. Bollards serve a dual purpose: (1) protecting the transformer from vehicle damage, and (2) preventing vehicles from parking or maneuvering too close to the electrical equipment. The absence of bollards at T2 violates this requirement.

comment: Multiple transformer pads appear to be located within 2 feet of concrete sidewalks per visual analysis of Sheet 9. Provide: (1) Updated site plan with dimension lines and callouts clearly documenting the distance from back of sidewalk to each transformer pad (T1, T2, T3, T4), confirming minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4, OR (2) Reposition transformers to achieve minimum 2-foot separation from all sidewalks, or (3) If clearance cannot be achieved, provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing reduced sidewalk clearance with specific approval conditions.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pads (T1, T2, T3, T4) relative to adjacent sidewalks and pedestrian paths
observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to measure distance from transformer pads to sidewalks and pedestrian paths. Vision analysis identified clearances for each transformer: 'T1: A Concrete Sidewalk wraps tightly around the eastern and northern sides of this pad. It appears to be within 2 feet of the pad. T2: A concrete sidewalk running north-south along the side of Bldg. 4 passes very close to the western edge of this pad (appears to be within 2 feet). T3: A concrete walkway runs east-west just north of the pad, connecting the driveway to Unit 604. It appears to be within 2 to 5 feet. T4: A concrete sidewalk runs north-south just to the east of the pad, leading to Unit 801. It appears to be within 2 feet.' Three of the four transformers (T1, T2, T4) are documented as being within 2 feet of sidewalks, which meets or may slightly exceed the 2-foot minimum. T3 is within 2-5 feet. No specific dimension lines, callouts, or clearance annotations are provided on the site plan to document compliance with the 2-foot setback requirement.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' The 'back of sidewalk' refers to the edge of the sidewalk surface farthest from the roadway or pedestrian area - essentially the inner edge of the sidewalk adjacent to property features. A 2-foot minimum separation is required to: (1) provide space for sidewalk maintenance and repair, (2) prevent sidewalk deterioration from transformer vibration or equipment settling, (3) ensure pedestrians are not placed in direct proximity to electrical equipment, and (4) allow for minor adjustments in sidewalk alignment during maintenance. Vision analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 are at or potentially at less than the 2-foot minimum. While T3 may be within acceptable range (2-5 feet is unclear - 'within 2 to 5 feet' could mean 2 feet or could mean 5 feet). The absence of specific dimension documentation on the site plan creates ambiguity. To comply with the requirement, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate the 2-foot setback is maintained. Estimated visual distances are insufficient for compliance verification.

comment: Many meter locations shown on Sheet 21 are not within sight of transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path (see EL-14.38 findings). Provide: (1) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design AND Distribution Metering business units authorizing meter locations without direct line of sight to transformers, OR (2) Reposition all meters to locations that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer on first floor/ground level per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple meter locations throughout the site
observation: Examined Sheet 21 to identify meter locations and access. Vision analysis identified: 'Locations: Meters are explicitly labeled as Electrical Meters using text boxes with leader lines. The leader lines point directly to the exterior walls of the buildings. Locations include: West side of Bldg. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8; East side of Bldg. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; South side of Bldg. 7.' The notations appear to place meters on first-floor/ground-level building faces.
reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 addresses 'Meters shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer, without written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units documented.' Two alternative compliance paths exist: (1) Meters are on first floor/ground level AND within sight of transformer (standard requirement), OR (2) Meters are not on first floor/ground level OR not within sight of transformer (exception scenario that requires written approval). The deficiency statement in EL-14.70 specifically addresses the exception case: 'when meters are shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer.' This triggers if either condition is not met. Vision analysis from EL-14.38 documented that 'many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer' because they are on opposite sides of buildings. This represents a failure of the 'within sight' requirement. The Regulatory Overview clarifies the requirement: 'Meter locations not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer require written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units.' The submitted plans show many meters without line of sight but provide no documented approval from AE Design or Distribution Metering. Therefore, EL-14.70 is a fail.

comment: Transformer locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Currently shown only on electrical plan (Sheet 21) and site plan (Sheet 9). Missing from wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan sheets.

The grouping guidance specifies that 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and elevation sheets)' and that 'grading and storm plans must also show transformers when those disciplines are affected by transformer placement or routing.' Omitting transformers from the wet utilities, landscape, and grading plans means these critical disciplines have not integrated the electrical infrastructure and cannot verify conflicts, clearances, or impacts.

comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its type: Pad-Mounted Transformer, Pole-Mounted Transformer, Vault, or Service Drop. Current labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' lack explicit type specification.

comment: Existing transformer pad shown on survey (Sheet 4) must be depicted and labeled as 'Existing' or 'EX' on all applicable plan sheets, with notation indicating whether it will be retained, removed, or replaced.

The ambiguous representation on Sheet 9 (with a single '(Typ.)' notation) does not align clearly with the four transformers shown on Sheet 21, creating confusion about the actual number and locations of transformers on the site.

comment: Transformer pad locations and 10-foot lateral clearance zones must be shown on the landscape plan to verify that tree locations comply with minimum required clearances from electrical equipment.

comment: Transformer clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 must be clearly shown on the electrical plan with dimension lines indicating minimum clearance distances from buildings, structures, obstacles, and access areas.

Vision analysis confirms: 'No clearance zones marked, No indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.' reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including 10-ft clearance for hot-stick use areas adjacent to open areas or buildings, 15-ft clearance when facing confined spaces, 3-5 ft clearances from ventilated obstructions, 20-ft clearance from fire escapes, 5-12 ft clearance from building walls depending on material, and no covering above. These clearances must be shown on plans with dimensions and notations to document compliance. Without clearance zones depicted, review agencies cannot verify that the site design accommodates these requirements.

Vertical profiles showing how electrical routing crosses or interfaces with storm drain, water, wastewater, and other buried infrastructure are essential for construction sequencing and conflict resolution.

This information is essential for Austin Energy design review and for construction coordination.

comment: Identify all curbing that falls within transmission easements or along transformer equipment pad access routes, and label as 'Laydown Curb' per UCM § 1.14.4.E and Austin Energy requirements. Show curb profiles and clearance dimensions for access.

Standard curbs impede equipment access. Sheet 3 Block 16 notes specify that grading near transmission structures must be coordinated with Austin Energy. Without showing the transformer access routes and identifying required laydown curb locations, it cannot be verified that the design accommodates Austin Energy truck access for equipment installation and maintenance.

comment: Show drivable access routes from the nearest parking/traffic area to each transformer pad, with dimensions indicating the distance. If distance exceeds 6 feet, show the dedicated access route design.
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) do not show drivable access routes to the transformer pad locations. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformers but does not indicate how Austin Energy trucks would access them for installation and maintenance. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Equipment pads must be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility unless otherwise approved by AE Design.' Without showing access routes, it cannot be verified that the transformer pads are accessible.
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad-mounted transformers require drivable access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. If a transformer is located more than 6 feet from an existing parking or traffic area, a dedicated access route must be provided and documented on the plans. Showing transformer locations without indicating access routes creates ambiguity about whether Austin Energy can reach the equipment for installation, operation, and maintenance.

comment: Provide profile view(s) showing how underground electrical routing crosses storm drain piping, including crossing location, elevation differences, separation distance, and any special protection required at crossing points.

comment: Show transformer pad door locations and control positions on the electrical plan, and indicate clearance zones appropriate to each side per UCM § 1.10.4 based on equipment orientation and adjacent features.

Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of door locations or designated clearance zones around the transformer pads.' The transformer pad symbols do not differentiate between different sides of the pad or indicate which side has the operating door and controls.
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, the clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers vary depending on the equipment side. Sides with operating controls/doors ('hot-stick use areas') require 10-15 ft clearance depending on whether they face open space or confined space. Sides without controls require 3-5 ft clearance. Showing the door location and control side is essential for proper site design to ensure the specified clearances are available on the correct sides of the equipment. Without this detail, compliance cannot be verified.

comment: Identify and show on plans a transformer-specific electrical easement with dimensions adequate to encompass the transformer pad location, all required clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side), and an access zone for Austin Energy operations and maintenance.
observation: Sheet 9, 11, and 21 show various electrical easements (5' Electric & Tele. Easement, 5' P.U.E., etc.) labeled with recording information. However, these easements are shown as property-line-based boundaries and do not specifically delineate easement areas around the transformer pad locations. The grouping guidance states: 'Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover specific facility clearances and access requirements' and references UCM § 1.3.24 (Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities). No easement dimensions are verified against the specific clearance requirements for the transformer pads themselves (which require clearances ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side and use).
reasoning: Austin Energy requires easements that are adequate in size to cover not only the physical location of electrical facilities but also the clearance zones and access areas required by code. The grouping notes state: 'There is no uniform "5-foot electrical easement" standard in Austin codes. Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover the physical location of facilities, required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side and configuration), and areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access per UCM § 1.3.24.' Without showing transformer-specific easement boundaries with dimensions verified against code clearance requirements, compliance cannot be confirmed.

observation: Vision analysis of all plan sheets confirms no transformer screening is shown. Sheet 21 electrical plan shows transformer pads as basic symbols with no screening details. This ensures that screening design does not interfere with required clearance zones or door operations, and allows Austin Energy to verify access compatibility. Screening details are also necessary for architectural and landscape integration review.

comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its size in kVA (e.g., '150 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer' or '300 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer').
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) labels the four transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size information. Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for design review, equipment ordering, and installation planning. Without size specifications, Austin Energy cannot verify that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project and cannot identify any shortfalls or required upgrades.

comment: Provide transformer pad dimensions (length × width × height where applicable) on all plans where transformers are shown, ensuring dimensions are consistent across sheets and adequate for the specified transformer kVA rating.

Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad clearance requirements depend partly on equipment size. Without documented pad dimensions, reviewing agencies cannot verify design adequacy or construction completeness.

comment: Label each transformer with its metering method (e.g., 'CT Metered' or 'Building Metered') to indicate how service measurement will be configured.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but provides no labeling indicating metering method. CT metering is used for larger transformer capacities (typically above 75 kVA), while building-level metering may be used for smaller loads. The metering method impacts the location of meter installation, the service distribution enclosure configuration, and the overall electrical service design. Without this specification, coordination with Austin Energy and proper electrical design cannot be completed.

comment: Meter locations must be shown and labeled on the site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan (Sheet 21).
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows eight meter locations on building exterior walls, with each labeled 'Electrical Meters.' reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.A, meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan). This allows all reviewing disciplines to verify meter accessibility, line of sight to transformers, separation from other utilities, and landscape or site features that might interfere with meter access or visibility. Omitting meters from the site and landscape plans means these disciplines have not verified meter integration with their designs.

comment: Show and label the existing meter (with 'EX' or 'Existing' notation) on the electrical plan, site plan, and landscape plan. Include notation indicating whether it will be abandoned, removed, or retained and integrated into the new service design.

Without showing the existing meter on the development plans, there is ambiguity about its status and how it relates to the new electrical service design.

comment: Clearly identify the service configuration: if meters are served from a single point of service, show the service distribution enclosure and disconnect locations grouped with the meters. If each building has an independent service point, note that on the plan.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters (one per building) on building exteriors but does not show any disconnects or service distribution enclosures. The grouping guidance states: 'When two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors, meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location with a service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway.' With 8 buildings and 8 individual meters, the grouping/point-of-service configuration is unclear. No legend or notes explain the service configuration.
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B, when multiple meters serve a single development, they must be coordinated as a grouped metering system if they share a point of service. If each building has its own individual service point, that must be clearly documented. Without showing disconnects and grouping configuration, it cannot be determined whether the design complies with grouped metering requirements.

comment: Show and label all service disconnects on the electrical plan. Indicate their location relative to meters (grouped together per code requirements) and verify they are within 20 feet and line of sight of the meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows and labels eight meter locations on building exterior walls as 'Electrical Meters.' However, no disconnects are shown, labeled, or identified on the electrical plan. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location... The disconnect must be grouped with the meter beside the AE transformer (adhering to transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4) or outside the building within line of sight of the transformer.'
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1 and 1.16.0, both meters AND disconnects must be shown and labeled on plans. The disconnect is where the customer's service is isolated from the utility service and is a critical safety component. Without showing disconnect locations, it cannot be verified that they are properly grouped with meters, within required distances, within line of sight of transformers, and accessible for emergency disconnection.

comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service (where Austin Energy service conductors connect to customer service equipment) on the electrical plan. This may be shown as a meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or other AE-approved location.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows service entry point labeled 'Underground Electric Line' at the western property boundary, transformers, pull boxes, and meters. This location also determines where disconnects and service distribution enclosures must be placed per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B. Without clear identification, design coordination and code compliance verification are incomplete.

comment: On the site plan (Sheet 9), clearly show existing power poles and electric lines, indicate which will be removed/relocated/retained, and show any new poles or overhead electric routing required for the development. Include Austin Energy coordination notes referencing removal approvals.
observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.'
