The development site plan should show existing poles, indicate which are to be removed or relocated, and show any new poles or routing required for the development. Without this coordination visible on the final site plan, contractors may not clearly understand the scope of electrical work required.

comment: Measure and show the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area. If any pad is within 4 feet, show bollard locations and spacing (minimum 4-inch galvanized rigid metal posts) designed to allow equipment door opening.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations but does not indicate distances to adjacent parking or driveway areas, nor are any bollards shown. No dimensions are provided that would allow verification of whether transformer pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas or outside this distance. Bollards protect the equipment from vehicle damage. Without measuring distances from transformer pads to parking areas and showing required bollards, it cannot be verified that the site design protects equipment or meets code requirements.

comment: Show transformer pad locations on the grading plan with spot elevations on all four sides of each pad, demonstrating that ground slopes direct drainage flow away from buildings and towards site drainage areas.
observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows site contours, retaining walls, and drainage features but does not indicate transformer pad locations or spot elevations around them. This is a critical safety and environmental requirement. The grading plan must show transformer locations with spot elevations on all sides of the pad demonstrating that slopes direct flow away from building foundations and towards site drainage. Without this detail, code compliance cannot be verified and environmental risks cannot be assessed.

comment: Show disconnect locations on the electrical plan and indicate the distance from each meter. Verify that meter-to-disconnect distance does not exceed 20 feet and that they are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exteriors and four transformers at various locations, but no disconnects are shown. Without showing disconnect locations, distances between meters and disconnects cannot be verified.
reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J, the meter-to-disconnect distance is limited to a maximum of 20 feet, and they must be within line of sight of each other. This ensures that the disconnect can be located quickly in an emergency and that the electrical service can be readily shut off. Without showing disconnects on the electrical plan, this code requirement cannot be reviewed or verified during plan check or construction.

It is possible that elevation sheets exist in a separate architectural drawing set not included in the primary site plan submission.

Without documented electrical load calculations and transformer capacity specifications, it cannot be verified that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer quantity not adequate to serve all buildings in development' as a potential deficiency. comment: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether switchgear is required for the four-transformer configuration. If switchgear is required, show its location and integrate it into the electrical plan with proper labeling and coordination notes.

The applicant's responsibility is to demonstrate this requirement is met by showing root barrier specifications on the plans. The complete absence of root barrier details is a failure to comply. While the grouping guidance notes that 'missing elements are deficiencies,' the presence of trees at these distances without the required accompanying root barrier specifications constitutes a failure to meet the code requirement. No assumption can be made that root barriers will be installed if not shown and specified on the plans.

comment: Root barrier construction details are completely absent from the landscape plans. Provide a detail sheet showing root barrier construction with minimum 4-foot depth and positioning exactly 5 feet from underground equipment edge, per UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements.
applicableAreas: Areas with trees proposed within 5-20 lateral feet of underground equipment
observation: Reviewed all landscape detail sheets (Sheets 31, 35, 37) and supporting documentation for root barrier specifications. Without a detail sheet showing depth and placement specifications, there is no means to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.10.4 root barrier requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from equipment edge).
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies precise requirements for root barriers: minimum 4 feet deep and positioned 5 feet from the equipment edge. The applicant must demonstrate this through detail drawings and/or plan notes. The complete absence of any root barrier detail or specification means the requirement cannot be verified. comment: Trees proposed near overhead electric line (southern boundary) have not been verified as utility-compatible species against ECM Appendix F. Verify all species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) in ECM Appendix F UC column and provide documentation. For any non-UC species within 15 feet of OHE, provide written Austin Energy approval.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line runs and trees are proposed within 15 lateral feet
observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 identified multiple trees (marked 'M' for mitigation trees) positioned along the southern property boundary. The sheet clearly shows the OHE (Overhead Electric) line labeled running the entire length of the southern boundary. Several proposed tree canopy circles visually overlap or are immediately tangent to the OHE line, with at least three 'M' trees having canopy circles crossing directly over the OHE line and utility pole symbols. From Sheet 32 (Tree List) and Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations), the proposed trees include Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud. However, ECM Appendix F (the definitive reference for Utility-Compatible species identification) is not provided in the site plan documentation. Without access to the UC column of ECM Appendix F, the utility-compatible status of these species cannot be verified. The grouping guidance explicitly states that UC designation must be verified by cross-reference with the UC column of Appendix F, not by assumption based on species name or size. No Austin Energy approval letter, coordination note, or design stamp indicating approval for non-UC species placement is visible on the landscape plans.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only utility-compatible (UC) trees be planted within 15 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment. The critical point is that UC status is definitive—only species with 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F qualify. The grouping guidance warns against common review errors: assuming all small trees are UC without Appendix F verification. Because Appendix F is not provided in the site plan, UC status cannot be determined from available evidence. Furthermore, the trees are positioned directly under the OHE line (southern boundary), which is within the 15-foot zone. Even if some species might be UC (Live Oak and Cedar Elm are typically UC), this cannot be confirmed without Appendix F. The fact that non-UC species may be among the proposed trees, combined with their proximity to the OHE line and lack of documented Austin Energy approval, constitutes a failure. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through documentation.

comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak both with mature heights ≥40 feet) are proposed along the southern property boundary within the overhead electric line corridor. These species must be maintained at least 25 lateral feet from the OHE line per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Revise landscape plan to show either: (1) relocation of large trees to maintain 25-foot clearance from OHE line, or (2) substitution with smaller species (mature height <40 feet).
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric distribution line runs
observation: Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) specifies proposed shade trees: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia) and 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), both specified as 100 GAL. container grown with 4' caliper and 16' height minimum. Standard references (landscape industry data, ECM Appendix F) list Cedar Elm and Live Oak with mature heights in the range of 40-50 feet or greater, placing both species in the 'large tree' category (≥40 feet mature height per grouping definition). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (M) positioned along the southern boundary where the OHE line is located. Vision analysis confirms at least three trees with canopy circles overlapping or directly tangent to the OHE line. No ECM Appendix F reference is provided in the site plan to definitively confirm mature height specifications, but based on standard horticultural data, both Cedar Elm and Live Oak commonly achieve or exceed 40 feet mature height. No verification that these large trees are positioned more than 25 feet from the overhead electric distribution line is evident on the landscape plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states: 'Large trees (mature height ≥40 feet) may not be planted within 25 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment.' The proposed large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak) are positioned directly along the OHE line at the southern boundary, well within 25 feet. The landscape plan does not show distance annotations or clearance verification. The applicant must demonstrate either (a) that the proposed trees are NOT large trees by providing mature height specifications from a qualified source (ECM Appendix F), or (b) that they are positioned more than 25 feet from the OHE line. Neither has been demonstrated. The conservative interpretation, given that both species are known to reach 40+ feet, is that large trees are proposed in violation of the 25-foot clearance requirement.

comment: No License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is evident for trees/landscaping proposed within electric easements. Before installation of any landscaping, irrigation, or trees within electric easement areas, obtain License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement and provide copy to City. Add plan note: 'License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement obtained prior to installation of landscaping within electric easement areas' [date/agreement number to be inserted].
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas (5' Electric Easements per Mecey Subdivision plat)
observation: Reviewed all landscape and supplementary documents for evidence of a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for trees proposed within electric easements. More critically, the landscape plans, site plans, and supplementary documents contain NO reference to a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement, NO plan notes stating 'License Agreement obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement,' and NO attached license agreement documentation. However, per UCM § 1.10.10.3, the agreement must be 'obtained and filed before the activity occurs,' and missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that before landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings are installed within electric easement areas, a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement must be obtained and filed. The applicant's responsibility at site plan stage is to demonstrate awareness of this requirement through either (a) a reference to an obtained license agreement (date and agreement number), or (b) a plan note committing to obtain the agreement before construction. Without such documentation, the reviewer cannot confirm the requirement will be met. The presence of proposed trees within or likely within electric easement areas, combined with the complete absence of license agreement documentation, constitutes a deficiency. The grouping guidance acknowledges license agreements may not be attached at early review but flags for verification—this is that flag. The applicant must either provide evidence of a license agreement or add a plan note committing to obtain one before construction/installation of any landscaping within the electric easements.

comment: Proposed trees are positioned within 10 lateral feet of overhead electric utility poles (southern boundary). Relocate trees to maintain minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from all utility poles, or provide distance callouts on landscape plan demonstrating compliance. applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along western and southern property boundaries
observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) labels and identifies utility poles with 'x' symbols positioned along the overhead electric (OHE) line. The burden of compliance is on the applicant to demonstrate the 10-foot clearance through either plan annotations (distance callouts) or relocation of trees. The visual evidence from the landscape plan suggests canopy overlap, which indicates non-compliance. Standard interpretation: if trees are not clearly shown to be at or beyond the 10-foot clearance distance, they are assumed to be in violation.

applicableAreas: Entire site for underground electric infrastructure
observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) contains a comprehensive site plan showing underground electric lines (blue lines), electrical pull boxes (circles), electrical transformer pads (squares), electrical meters on all buildings, overhead electric lines (OHE), and associated easements. The plan is detailed and clearly labeled. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at the same scale (1" = 20') shows building footprints, parking areas, trees, shrubs, contours, water lines (W), storm drain lines (SD), and overhead electric (OHE) line. HOWEVER, Sheet 31 does NOT show the underground electric facilities visible on Sheet 21: no underground electric lines, no pull boxes, no transformer pads are depicted on the landscape plan. The notation on Sheet 31 lists 'Utility lines such as water (W), storm drain (SD), and overhead electric (OHE)' per the vision analysis, confirming that while OHE is shown, underground electric infrastructure is not. This is a coordination gap: the landscape plan cannot show proper tree clearance verification for underground utilities if those utilities are not depicted.
reasoning: The grouping guidance emphasizes: 'A requirement met on the grading plan may still be missing from pond plan sheets, profile sheets, or detail sheets. If a requirement applies to multiple sheets, finding it on one sheet does not constitute a pass—verify each relevant sheet independently.' This is a coordination requirement: for landscape planners and reviewers to verify clearances between trees and Austin Energy facilities, those facilities must be shown on the landscape plan. The grouping requires 'Landscape Plans - Tree and shrub locations, species, mature sizes, mature canopy spread, root barrier details' and 'Utility Plans - Underground electric facilities routing, duct banks, vaults, manholes, transformer pads.' When electric utilities are shown on utility/electrical plans but NOT on landscape plans, the reviewer cannot verify compliance with clearance requirements. This is a classic coordination deficiency: missing information on a required plan that prevents compliance verification.

comment: Trees proposed within restricted zones relative to overhead electric facilities (under OHE line, near utility poles) lack documented Austin Energy written approval. Any variation from UCM § 1.10.10.4 clearance or species requirements requires explicit Austin Energy approval. Provide one of the following: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email with date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design approval stamp on plans. Alternatively, relocate trees to comply with required clearances without variation.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within clearance-restricted zones (under/near OHE line, near poles)
observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 shows mitigation trees (M) positioned directly along the southern property boundary where the OHE line runs, with canopy circles overlapping the OHE line and utility pole symbols. Sheet 35 identifies the proposed species: Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud. Based on standard horticultural data, Live Oak and Cedar Elm are large trees (≥40 feet mature height). Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud are smaller species (20-25 feet typically). The landscape plan shows trees positioned under/near the OHE line without (a) distance annotations demonstrating >15 feet (for non-UC species) or >25 feet (for large trees) clearance, or (b) explicit notation of Austin Energy approval, Austin Energy Design stamp, or attached approval letter/email. The grouping guidance lists 'Missing Austin Energy written approval for variations' as a common violation pattern: 'Landscape plans show trees within restricted zones (e.g., within 15 feet of overhead distribution, within 5 feet of underground equipment) without documented Austin Energy approval letter, email, or plan note.' This situation matches that pattern. The trees are within restricted zones relative to the OHE line, and no Austin Energy approval is documented.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that any variation from the planting distances or species requirements requires explicit written approval from Austin Energy. The grouping identifies acceptable documentation forms: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation. None of these appear on the landscape plans. The trees shown under/near the OHE line represent a variation from standard clearance requirements (they are within 15 feet of overhead distribution, and some appear to be within or adjacent to utility pole locations). Without documented Austin Energy approval for this variation, the requirement is not met. Per the grouping: 'Acceptable documentation includes: Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date in plan notes; Plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative; Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation.' The complete absence of such documentation, combined with trees positioned in restricted zones, constitutes a deficiency.

comment: Proposed tree species cannot be verified as utility-compatible without ECM Appendix F. Provide either: (1) a copy of ECM Appendix F with UC column marked for all proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud), or (2) a letter from City forester confirming UC status of each species. Species shown near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary) must be verified as having 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: All areas where proposed trees are within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution or 50 feet of overhead transmission
observation: Sheet 35 lists proposed tree species: Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia), Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora secundiflora), and Mexican Redbud (Cercis canadensis var. mexicana). Both common names and scientific names are provided, which allows cross-reference against ECM Appendix F. However, the site plan documentation does NOT include ECM Appendix F itself. The grouping guidance emphasizes: 'Cross-reference proposed tree species (common or scientific name from landscape plan) against ECM Appendix F table. Only species with x in the UC column qualify as utility-compatible.' And: 'Common review errors to avoid: Assuming all small trees (<20 feet) are UC without verifying UC column.' Without access to the actual ECM Appendix F document, the UC status of these species cannot be definitively determined from the site plan alone. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows some trees positioned near the overhead electric line (southern boundary) where utility-compatible species are required (within 15 feet of OHE). While Live Oak and Cedar Elm are commonly known to be utility-compatible species in Austin practice, this should be verified against the actual Appendix F table, not assumed. Texas Mountain Laurel is noted in the grouping regulatory overview as a possible UC species (25-foot example), but again, definitive verification requires Appendix F.
reasoning: The issue is evidentiary: the applicant must provide proof that species used near electric facilities comply with the UC requirement. Proof consists of either (a) ECM Appendix F included in the site plan documentation with UC column marked for each species, or (b) a reference letter from the City's urban forester or landscape code reviewer confirming UC status. The site plan provides species names but not the definitive Appendix F verification. While it is likely that Live Oak and Cedar Elm are UC (they are well-known compatible species), the grouping guidance explicitly warns against assumption. Without the Appendix F document in the site plan set, the UC status is 'unclear'—which under the review protocol means it cannot be confirmed. This becomes a 'fail' if any trees shown near electric facilities are later found (via Appendix F review) to be non-UC. For now, it is 'unclear' because the species names alone, without Appendix F, are insufficient proof of compliance.

comment: Point of service (POS) location is not explicitly labeled on any required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure but lacks a clear 'Point of Service' designation. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately identify the POS. Add explicit POS labeling to Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing where Austin Energy infrastructure connects to proposed customer infrastructure.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and meters, but does NOT contain an explicit label designating the Point of Service (POS). The plan shows where proposed underground electric lines enter from Valley View Road (western property line) and connect to electrical pull boxes, but the specific connection point to Austin Energy infrastructure is not labeled as 'Point of Service' or 'POS'. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only a single 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying the POS or primary source. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines on boundaries but no identification of POS. The grouping's regulatory overview (UCM § 1.16.0) requires the POS to be clearly designated, and unless otherwise specified by Austin Energy, the POS must be shown on the required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans).
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) and § 1.4.2.6 require that the point of service designation be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans). While Sheet 21 depicts the general electrical routing and infrastructure, the POS is not explicitly labeled or designated. Without clear labeling of the POS location, a reviewer cannot confirm compliance with the requirement to show the 'desired point of electric service' on the plans. This is distinct from merely showing infrastructure; the POS must be explicitly identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors connect or terminate per UCM § 1.3.4.

comment: Underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required 'all utilities' plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add underground electric line routing, conduit paths, and service connections to both sheets showing how power is distributed from the source (Valley View Road connection) to the transformer pads and to building meters.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows underground electric line routing with blue lines, conduit connections, and pull box locations. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show underground electric cabling routing despite being required as a sheet showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 9 displays other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain) with clear line designations but shows only a single transformer pad without any underground electrical lines routing from the source to that pad or to the buildings. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) similarly does NOT show underground electric line routing; it only shows overhead electric (OHE) lines on the western boundary and contains no depiction of the proposed underground electric service lines serving the development. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes a legend entry for 'Underground Electric' but the lines are not actually drawn on the plan view.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations to be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains detailed electrical routing, the deficiency is that this information must be replicated on the site plan and landscape plan as required plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is identified as showing 'all utilities' but lacks the underground electrical routing information. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) is a required plan sheet per the grouping's regulatory overview but contains no underground electrical infrastructure. Absence of this information on sheets identified as showing utilities constitutes non-compliance, even if the information exists elsewhere in the plan set.

comment: Transformer pad locations are not shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite this being a required plan sheet per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add transformer pad symbols and labels to Sheet 31 matching those shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to ensure complete infrastructure coordination across all utility plan sheets.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows two transformer pad locations with explicit labels and symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' near the main entrance (west side, south of Bldg. 2/8 area). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), identified as a required plan sheet showing utilities, does NOT show transformer locations at all. The vision analysis confirmed that Sheet 31 contains no transformer pad symbols, labels, or indications. The landscape plan shows drainage basins and utility line designations (OHE, SD, W) but is completely absent of transformer pad information.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires transformer locations to be shown on all required plan sheets: site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. Sheet 21 (electrical plan) and Sheet 9 (site plan) both show transformers, but Sheet 31 (landscape plan) does not. The landscape plan is explicitly listed as a required plan sheet in the grouping's 'Documents to Review' section and the grouping's regulatory overview states that Sheet 31 is required. Omitting transformer locations from the landscape plan violates the requirement to show infrastructure consistently across all required sheets. This is not a redundancy issue; it is a compliance requirement that all required sheets must contain the relevant infrastructure information for complete coordination.

comment: Electric meter locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required plan sheets. Add meter locations to both sheets showing where all electrical meters are positioned on the building exteriors, consistent with the locations shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21).
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electric meter locations clearly labeled as 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors (north walls of Bldgs. 1, 3, 4, 5; south walls of Bldgs. 6, 7; west walls of Bldgs. 2, 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not display meter locations - the vision analysis found no meter symbols or labels on this sheet despite it being identified as showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also does not show meter locations. The meters are confined to Sheet 21 only, and absent from the two required plan sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) that must show utility infrastructure per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 (Point of Service definition) and UCM § 1.4.2.6 (Customer Drawings Specifications) require electric meter locations to be shown on all required plan sheets including the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains this information, the requirement specifies that the information must appear on the site plan and landscape plan. Absence of meter locations from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not adequately document the electrical service infrastructure for review. This prevents verification of meter grouping, spacing, and coordination with other site elements per the meter requirements in UCM § 1.5.2.1(G).

comment: Poles and service drops are not clearly shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add pole locations and service drop routing to this sheet to demonstrate coordination with site grading, landscaping, and building placement. Show specific utility pole locations and how overhead or underground service is routed to serve the development.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows poles and service routing via overhead electric lines on the western boundary (OHE designation) and underground routing throughout the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines along boundaries (OHE designation) but limited detail on service routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines along the southern boundary but does NOT show any specific poles or service drop locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirmed: 'While an Overhead Electric (OHE) line is shown along the bottom perimeter, specific utility poles are not distinctly labeled, nor are service drops routing power from the main line to the individual buildings.' The landscape plan is deficient in showing poles and service infrastructure details.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires poles or service drops to be shown on all required plan sheets including the landscape plan. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) is explicitly listed as a required plan sheet per the grouping's documents to review and regulatory overview. While Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line designation (OHE), it does not show specific pole locations or service drop routing to buildings. This omission prevents verification of clearances to structures, vegetation conflicts, and proper utility coordination. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically notes 'Incomplete infrastructure across sheets: Electric infrastructure shown on site plan but omitted from landscape plan or electrical plans, violating the requirement to show infrastructure consistently across all required sheets.'

comment: Projected electrical load is not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or any other plan sheet. Add projected electrical service amperage, estimated demand (kW or kVA), or connected load to the electrical design plan. Include load calculations for all buildings and identify the service voltage and amperage for the development.
observation: Examination of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows detailed electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground routing, benchmarks, utility notes) but contains NO indication of projected electrical load in any form. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 lists 'Utility Notes' that address contractor requirements and material specifications, but no load information. The 'Key values' section at the beginning of the guide lists building sizes and floor areas but no electrical load figures (kW, kVA, Amps, or service amperage). The sheet's 'Utility Notes' block discusses verification of existing utilities and private water/wastewater specifications but contains no electrical load data. No supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report) contain electrical load information.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires 'projected electrical load' to be shown on plan sheets. This is distinguished from infrastructure location - load information must be documented to allow Austin Energy to verify adequate service capacity and equipment sizing. The absence of any load figures (service amperage, estimated demand, connected load, or design load) on Sheet 21 prevents verification of transformer sizing, conductor capacity, and service adequacy. Without projected load documentation, Austin Energy cannot make an informed determination of line extension requirements, duct bank requirements, vault vs. pedestal service selection, or service point location per UCM § 1.3.12 and § 1.5.2.1.

comment: Service type (overhead or underground) is not clearly designated on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add a clear note or legend entry on each required plan sheet stating the service type (e.g., 'Proposed Service: Underground Electric Distribution' or similar) to eliminate ambiguity and ensure all required sheets clearly identify whether the development uses overhead, underground, or mixed service type.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly designates the service type as UNDERGROUND through explicit labels 'Underground Electric Line' pointing to the routing, blue line styling, and underground pull box locations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows both existing overhead electric (OHE) on the western boundary AND proposed transformer pad, but the relationship between these and the service type is ambiguous - is the service overhead from the OHE source into an underground distribution on site? Or is there both overhead and underground proposed? The sheet does not explicitly state 'Service Type: Underground' or similar designation. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines on the southern boundary but provides no clarity on the overall service type for the development. A reviewer examining Sheets 9 and 31 cannot definitively determine whether the development is served by overhead service, underground service, or a combination without cross-referencing Sheet 21.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires service type (overhead or underground) to be 'clearly designated' on plans. While Sheet 21 makes this clear through labeling and line styling, the requirement is for the designation to appear on all required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and electrical plans). Sheets 9 and 31 do not clearly designate the overall service type. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically lists 'Service type ambiguity: Plans show both overhead and underground elements without clearly designating which service type applies.' A plan reviewer examining the site plan and landscape plan should be able to immediately determine the service type without referencing other sheets.

comment: Proposed electrical easement locations and extents for the new underground electric distribution are not clearly delineated or dimensioned on the electrical design plan. Add easement boundaries and dimensions showing the width and extent of the easement(s) required to accommodate the proposed underground electric routing, transformers, and infrastructure within the site. Verify easement widths meet Austin Energy requirements for maintenance and future replacement.
observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements on the perimeter: '10' P.U.E.' (west), '5' P.U.E.' (north), '15' Easement' and '5' Electric Easement' (east), '5' Elec. Easement' (south). These are dimensioned and labeled around the property boundary. However, the vision analysis noted: 'There are no dimensions or distinct easement boundaries drawn specifically for the internal, proposed underground electrical routing (blue lines) throughout the center of the site.' The grouping's regulatory overview states that UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires showing 'electrical easements' - this includes not only existing/dedicated easements on the plat but also proposed easements for new infrastructure. The internal underground electric line routing (blue lines on Sheet 21) does not have an associated proposed easement boundary shown or dimensioned. The extent of the underground electric easement serving the two transformer pads and internal routing is not delineated or dimensioned on the plan.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires 'electrical easement locations and extents' to be clearly delineated on plans. The vision analysis and grouping's common violation patterns note 'Electrical easement omissions: Existing or proposed electrical easements not shown or not dimensioned, violating UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i).' While the site plan shows plat-dedicated easements around the perimeter, the proposed easement(s) needed for the new underground electrical infrastructure serving the transformers and internal routing are not explicitly delineated with boundaries or dimensions. An easement width is not specified for the proposed underground electric distribution serving the development.

comment: One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser is not included in the plan set. Provide a complete one-line diagram showing the electrical service configuration including main service entrance, distribution panel(s), protective devices, branch circuits, and load distribution per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. The diagram must clearly show how the service from Austin Energy connects to the customer's electrical system and distributes power throughout the development.
observation: Review of the site plan sheets (1-39) and supplementary documents reveals NO One-Line Diagram of an electrical riser included in the plan set. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows site layout, transformers, and routing but does not contain a one-line diagram. The README documentation lists all 39 sheets of the primary site plan, with Sheet 21 described as showing 'Layout of preliminary electrical design, routing, transformers, and meters' - this describes a site plan view, not a riser one-line diagram. No other electrical schematic or one-line diagram is mentioned in the sheet index. The supplementary documents (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report, etc.) do not reference a one-line diagram. The grouping's regulatory overview explicitly lists 'Missing One-Line Diagram: Plan set does not include One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser required by Table 1.4.3.B' as a common violation pattern.
reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B (Customer Drawings Specifications) explicitly requires 'One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser' as a mandatory component of the plan set. This is not optional and is a separate submittal from the site plan sheets. The one-line diagram must show the electrical service configuration, including service entrance, main distribution panel, branch circuits, protective devices, and load breakdown per building or service point. The absence of this document from the plan set is a clear violation of the requirement. The grouping's regulatory overview notes this is a required plan sheet per Table 1.4.3.B.

comment: Clarification needed regarding the two transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 and whether they represent separate services with different voltages. Provide Austin Energy documentation (ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement) confirming whether the two transformers are part of a single point of service at one voltage, or whether exceptions to UCM § 1.16.0(5) have been approved for multiple service points or voltages. If the transformers are step-down stages of a single service, add labeling to Sheet 21 clarifying the service configuration and voltage(s).
observation: Sheet 21 shows two electrical transformer pads, which may indicate two service points, but the vision analysis and detailed examination do not reveal explicit documentation of service voltage or whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved. The plan shows: 'Two proposed transformers shown, and both are explicitly designated as pad-mounted. One is located on the western side of the property...The second is located on the eastern side of the property.' The question is whether these two transformers serve different buildings with different voltages (which would violate the one-voltage rule) or whether they are both serving the same development at the same voltage (which would be acceptable step-down transformers). The blocks.md for Sheet 21 does not specify the voltage(s) for each transformer. No documentation from Austin Energy (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement) was provided that would confirm whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved.
reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) allows 'only one point of service and one service voltage' unless exceptions are 'approved by Austin Energy Design.' The presence of two transformers on the plan is not inherently a violation if they are both part of a single service point and serve the same voltage. However, without explicit documentation of the service voltage and Austin Energy approval for the transformer configuration, it cannot be verified whether the requirement is met. The grouping's regulatory overview states: 'Several infrastructure requirements cannot be determined from site plan review alone and require formal determination by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process' and specifically lists 'Vaults and pedestals: Service type selection is made during AE Design coordination and documented in Letter of Agreement or ESPA approval.' Similarly, the one-POS/one-voltage requirement requires Austin Energy confirmation. This item cannot be marked pass without evidence of AE approval, nor can it be marked fail without evidence of AE non-compliance.

comment: Austin Energy Notes section lacks required disclaimer stating that electric facilities are conceptual, preliminary in nature, not for bidding purposes, and subject to change during Austin Energy's final design review. Please add statement: 'Electric facilities shown are conceptual in nature and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown and may require changes to the site plan.'
observation: Sheet 3 contains two electric notes sections: a labeled 'Electric Notes' section with five notes addressing tree pruning, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and relocation of facilities. A visual inspection of these notes and the 'Electric Transmission Notes' section below them confirms the absence of any disclaimer language indicating that the electric facilities shown are conceptual, preliminary in nature, not intended for bidding purposes, or subject to change by Austin Energy during final design. The Electric Notes section contains operational and safety requirements but does not include the required disclaimer statement.
reasoning: The checklist item requires a note stating that 'electric facilities shown are conceptual only, should not be used for bidding purposes, and that final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown and may require changes to site plan.' This disclaimer is necessary to set expectations about the preliminary nature of electric facilities and Austin Energy's final design authority. The absence of this disclaimer represents a deficiency in plan documentation. The notes present address operational requirements but do not provide the required conceptual/preliminary design disclaimer.

comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note requiring Austin Energy review of any changes affecting electric requirements. Please add statement: 'Austin Energy must review any changes to plans that may affect electric requirements, including changes in building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, and spoil site locations.'
observation: The 'Electric Notes' section on Sheet 3 contains five notes addressing tree work rights, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. No note is present requiring coordination with Austin Energy or notification to Austin Energy of changes that may affect electric requirements. The notes do not list the specific change types (building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, spoil site locations) that require Austin Energy review.
reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires notification to Austin Energy when changes are proposed that may affect electric service requirements. This requirement protects both the applicant and Austin Energy by ensuring that significant site changes do not invalidate the preliminary electric design shown on plans. The grouping specifies that this note must identify specific change types including building square footage, building location, detention facilities, grading, and spoil sites. The absence of this coordination requirement note is a deficiency that could result in unapproved changes during construction.

comment: The section heading must read exactly 'Austin Energy Notes,' not 'Electric Notes' or other variations. Please change the section heading from 'Electric Notes' to 'Austin Energy Notes' on Sheet 3. Transmission-specific notes should be in a separate section headed 'Austin Energy Transmission Notes.'
observation: Sheet 3 contains two electric-related note sections. The first section heading reads 'Electric Notes' (not 'Austin Energy Notes'). The second section heading reads 'Electric Transmission Notes' (not 'Austin Energy Transmission Notes'). Neither section uses the required standard heading 'Austin Energy Notes.' A review of the General Site Plan Notes document requirements indicates the heading must use the exact text 'Austin Energy Notes' without variations such as 'Electric Notes,' 'Utility Notes,' 'City of Austin Electric Notes,' or similar.
reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document specifies required headings and warns that 'Changing the required text in your plan set will result in rejection of the application.' The heading 'Austin Energy Notes' is a standard, required element that helps contractors and developers identify the authority requiring the notes and ensures consistency with other project documentation. Using alternative headings such as 'Electric Notes' or 'Utility Notes' creates ambiguity about which utility the notes address. This is a formatting deficiency that affects plan clarity and compliance.

comment: Austin Energy Notes section appears twice on Sheet 3 (as 'Electric Notes' and as a duplicate unheaded block). Please consolidate all notes into a single 'Austin Energy Notes' section and remove the duplicate unheaded block below the Transmission Notes section.
observation: Sheet 3 contains the Austin Energy notes twice: First, as a labeled 'Electric Notes' section with five notes (tree pruning, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, relocation). Second, as an unheaded text block below the 'Electric Transmission Notes' section that contains identical content—five unnumbered paragraphs that are exact duplicates of the notes in the labeled section above. The duplicate block appears without a section heading and repeats notes already presented, creating redundancy on the same sheet.
reasoning: Plan clarity and professional organization require that standard note sections appear once on a plan set. When the same notes appear multiple times on a single sheet, it creates confusion about which version is the controlling set of requirements and increases the likelihood of conflicting or inconsistent information during construction. The checklist specifically flags this as a reviewer convention deficiency. Duplicate sections should be consolidated into a single 'Austin Energy Notes' section to avoid ambiguity.

comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and installation. Please add: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, including installation of conductors if determined during design (prior to building permit issuance) that developer will fund conductor installation. Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts. All costs for these improvements are the applicant's responsibility.'
observation: The Austin Energy notes on Sheet 3 include five notes addressing tree work, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. None of the notes present includes developer responsibility for designing and constructing conduit infrastructure or reference to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The grouping identifies that Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical routing and infrastructure, indicating that conduit infrastructure is a component of this project. No note is present establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and construction per current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards.
reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes basic requirements for electric distribution service, including developer-installed conduit when applicable. The required note must establish that: (1) the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, (2) the developer may be responsible for conductor installation if it is determined during design that developer funding is appropriate, (3) the developer must coordinate with other utilities to resolve conflicts, and (4) all costs are the applicant's responsibility. The current reference to 'Design Criteria Manual' (not outdated standards) is essential. Absence of this note creates ambiguity about developer responsibilities during construction.

comment: Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy has not been obtained. Site plan is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and is in first-round comment response phase. An approved/stamped electrical site plan with documented Austin Energy approval letter must be submitted prior to site plan approval, demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).
observation: The site plan submittal is at the first-round comment response phase (SP-2025-0126C submitted 05/20/2025). The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements through a Bluebeam markup link and lists multiple UCM sections that must be addressed (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4). However, no signed Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, or formal approval documentation is visible in the supplementary documents reviewed. Sheet 1 (Cover) shows empty approval stamp boxes with no Austin Energy approval date recorded. The electrical site plan (Sheet 21) is labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no indication of Austin Energy Design sign-off. The site is within Austin jurisdiction, has electrical service shown (transformers, meters, underground lines), and is clearly within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components per the electrical infrastructure layout shown on Sheet 21.
reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy prior to site plan approval. The grouping narrative states that Austin Energy approval demonstrates compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, which is adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual. Evidence of preliminary design comments from Austin Energy exists (Master Comment Report references Bluebeam markup), but no formal approval letter or stamped approval documentation is visible. The site plan status indicates it is still awaiting first-round comment response, which means Austin Energy approval has not yet been obtained. The site clearly requires Austin Energy service (electrical infrastructure is shown throughout the site plan) and falls within the mandatory approval trigger (within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components, in fact showing new customer connections).
